title: Landfall and Provision
premise: Astrid Reyes, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries after a client's death she may or may not have caused, takes one last job escorting a dying prospector named Efraim Voss to a hospital town. Instead, Voss trades her a hand-drawn map of the Serrano River's forbidden headwaters for a promise: carry his findings to the source before the mining consortium that killed his partner erases all evidence. Astrid, joined by Voss's estranged daughter Ines and a disgraced river pilot called Mabry, fights rapids, altitude, and the consortium's hired men upstream toward a glacial valley holding both a lost expedition's remains and proof that could clear Astrid's name — or bury her deeper. At the source, Astrid must choose between destroying the evidence to save Ines's life and delivering it to redeem her own; she chooses Ines, but Mabry secretly preserves a copy, and in the aftermath the truth surfaces anyway, clearing Astrid at the cost of everything she thought belonging required.
about_author: Paloma Ishikawa is a former wilderness first-responder who spent six seasons leading expeditions in Patagonia and the Karakoram before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels from a cabin outside Haines, Alaska, where she still guides part-time and keeps a wall of maps annotated with stories that never made it home.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Astrid Reyes crosses a border town under a false name, taking a low-paying medical escort job because no outfitter will hire a guide blacklisted twice. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: weary pragmatism masking grief over the client whose death ended her career.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Ledger
chapters.summary: Her client, prospector Efraim Voss, deteriorates faster than expected and reveals he isn't going to any hospital — he's going upstream. He shows her a map of the Serrano headwaters, closed by decree since a 1998 expedition vanished. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity kindling beneath exhaustion.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: Voss offers the map in exchange for a promise: reach the source before the Cordillera Extraction Group finishes its survey season and seals the valley forever. Astrid refuses; then consortium agents search their hotel, and refusal stops being safe. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Fleeing the agents, they shelter with Voss's estranged daughter Ines, a hydrologist who hasn't spoken to him in nine years. She agrees to come only to keep him alive long enough to answer for her mother's death on that same river. POV: alternating Astrid/Ines. Emotional beat: resentment braided with unfinished love.

chapters.title: Mabry's Boat
chapters.summary: In a riverport slum they hire Mabry, a pilot banned after running supplies for the very consortium now hunting them. His boat, the Provision, is half rust and half luck. First night on the water, agents torch the dock behind them. POV: Mabry. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption through motion.

chapters.title: Rapids at Redbank
chapters.summary: The first gorge nearly swamps them; Astrid's rope work saves Ines from drowning, earning a fragile trust. Voss's condition worsens; he begins confusing Astrid with his dead partner. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: competence as a language of care.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Camped in flooded timber, Ines finds 1998 expedition debris — a child's boot, a corroded radio. She confronts Voss about her mother; he confesses only fragments. Downstream, a consortium patrol boat passes with floodlights sweeping the banks. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: grief demanding answers the dying can't give.

chapters.title: The Portage
chapters.summary: A three-day portage around an unrunnable falls tests everyone: Voss must be carried, Mabry's shoulder gives out, and Astrid realizes the agents are tracking their satellite beacon. She makes the call to smash it and navigate blind. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: leadership as lonely arithmetic.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Stormbound, food short, the group fractures — Mabry wants to turn back, Ines accuses Voss of using them all as cover for his obsession. Voss slips into delirium and names the source: La Cuna, the Cradle. POV: Mabry. Emotional beat: the price of survival measured in trust spent.

chapters.title: The Ambush at Serpent Bend
chapters.summary: Consortium mercenaries catch them in a narrow bend; Mabry runs the boat through rapids he swore were suicide rather than surrender. They escape with a bullet-grazed hull and a prisoner's radio, learning the consortium wants the map, not them — yet. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Efraim's Confession
chapters.summary: Knowing he won't survive the journey, Voss tells the whole truth: the 1998 expedition was murdered to hide an untapped aquifer, his partner among the dead, and the map was drawn by the sole survivor — Ines's mother, who died trying to expose it. POV: Voss (final chapter in his voice). Emotional beat: absolution sought too late, granted anyway.

chapters.title: Burial Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: They bury Voss on a moraine overlooking the river he loved. Ines reads no eulogy, only the coordinates of the source aloud, making his grave a waypoint. The group, smaller and quieter, goes on. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: mourning converted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Leaving the boat, they climb into country no map admits exists — glacier, scree, thin air. Astrid's old injury flares; she hides a worsening limp. Behind them, helicopters mark the consortium closing in. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the body's honesty against the will's denial.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: A storm pins them to a cliff face for two days. Rations gone, Ines and Astrid trade histories in the dark — the client Astrid lost, the mother Ines lost — and discover both deaths were the same story: inconvenient people erased by convenient terrain. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: two guilts recognizing each other.

chapters.title: La Cuna
chapters.summary: They reach the source: a hidden glacial valley where the 1998 camp lies preserved in ice, along with survey documents proving the aquifer and the murders. The helicopters arrive overhead. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Source
chapters.summary: Mercenaries descend. Their commander offers a trade: burn the evidence and walk free, or be buried with it. A crevasse collapse traps Ines during the firefight; saving her means abandoning the documents to the flames already spreading. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the promise versus the person.

chapters.title: Provision
chapters.summary: Astrid chooses Ines, hauling her from the ice as the evidence burns — and Mabry, unseen, cuts the key core sample and field notebook from the cache and stows them aboard the battered Provision. They escape downriver through smoke. POV: Mabry. Emotional beat: quiet theft as an act of faith.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Running the river at flood stage, pursued, they outrun the mercenaries only by passing through a canyon the consortium needs intact — witnesses are dangerous there. They reach the delta as news breaks of a 'survey accident' in the headwaters. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: survival without victory.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: In the capital, Mabry reveals what he saved. Ines, a hydrologist's credentials finally meaning something, authenticates the data; a journalist and a prosecutor take it from there. Astrid expects nothing for herself — until the file includes the 2016 incident report that exonerates her. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, undeserved and real.

chapters.title: Reckonings
chapters.summary: Hearings, headlines, restitution. Astrid's blacklist dissolves; the consortium's officers fall. But Astrid finds vindication hollow without the wilderness, and Ines finds her mother's name restored to the record she died for. They meet at Voss's grave to decide what comes next. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: belonging redefined as chosen company, not cleared reputation.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: One year later: Astrid, Ines, and Mabry run a small guiding outfit on the Serrano's lower reaches, taking clients the big firms reject. The headwaters remain closed — protected now, not hidden. On the anniversary of Voss's burial, they plant a cairn marker at his moraine. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: home built from shared scars.

chapters.title: The River Remembers
chapters.summary: Final image: a new client asks Astrid if the wilderness ever forgives. She answers that it doesn't — it remembers, and so do we, and that's why some things are worth carrying upstream. The Provision pushes off into the current. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept, the journey continuing.
